texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} writes in {FACTION}'s name to ask the colony for two of its builders for a few days, with pay: the town has the timber to build again, and not the hands.

[storm,their:lowtech] A rider from {PLACE} says the storm two nights ago took the thatch off half the town and brought a barn down on its own cattle. {FACTION} have timber enough, but not the hands who know how to raise a roof truss that stays up.\n\nCould the colony lend two of its builders for a few days? {A_nameDef}'s name came up.

[storm,their:hightech] {FACTION}'s letter from {PLACE} is short. The windstorm took the roofs off the school and the clinic, and the town's own builders are working on the houses. They are asking the colony for two people who can frame and roof, for a day or two, and they will pay for it.

[fire,their:lowtech] Fire went down a row of houses at {PLACE} in the dry spell, and {FACTION} have cleared the ash and stacked new timber. What they lack is builders. They ask for two of the colony's, for a few days at the walls, and they will pay in silver and in goods of their own making.

[fire,their:hightech] Half of a street at {PLACE} burned out last week, and {FACTION} have the materials and the money to put it back. What they don't have is people who can build. Two of the colony's builders for a day or two would let them start before the weather turns.

[their:empire] A herald of the Empire at {PLACE} presents the compliments of the town's knight and asks a service: two builders of the colony to help raise the hall that came down, for a day and a half. The Empire pays its builders, the herald says, and remembers its friends.
[their:friend] "Send {FRIEND_nameDef} if you can," the letter from {PLACE} ends, after the part about the roofs. {FACTION} need two builders for a few days, and they trust the colony's.

li.label: Send builders to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider went home to say the colony's builders are coming.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to raise their roofs with the hands they have.

terms.li: At least two of the colony's people who can build (Construction 5 or more), at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away), staying about a day and a half while the roofs go back on. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll come home with about {COUNT} silver and a gift of the town's making, and {FACTION} will remember who came. Half the stay earns half the silver.

accepted.li: The colony will send builders to {PLACE}. Form a caravan with at least two who can build, and send it there.

ready.li: The colony's builders have reached {PLACE} and gone straight up onto the first roof. Keep the caravan there while they work.
[fire] The colony's builders are at {PLACE}, setting out the new walls along the burned street. Keep the caravan there while they work.

reminder.li: The roofs at {PLACE} are still open to the sky, and the colony's builders haven't come.

done.li: [worked] The last truss went up at {PLACE} and the colony's builders came down to a supper in the new hall. They're coming home with silver in their purses and a gift of the town's making in the packs.

[worked,their:empire] The hall at {PLACE} stands again, and the knight came down to thank the colony's builders in person, as the Empire's honour asks. They're coming home with silver and a gift of the town's.
[partial] The colony's builders put up what they could at {PLACE} before they had to go. {FACTION} paid them half and thanked them honestly.

fail.li: [missed] No builders came from the colony, and {PLACE} is still sleeping under tarps and broken rafters. {FACTION} know who said they would come.

cancelled.li: The roofs at {PLACE} no longer need the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.

texts.li: [host] A letter from {HOST} at {PLACE}, in a hurried hand: a sickness is going through the town, their own healer is down with it, and {HOST} asks the colony to lend its healer for two days.

[fever,their:tribal] A runner from {PLACE} squats at the gate to get breath. A fever is going through the longhouses of {FACTION}, and their own healer is lying in one of them. They ask for the colony's healer, {A_nameDef} or another, for two days at the bedsides.

[fever,their:medieval] {FACTION}'s rider from {PLACE} carries a letter sealed in a hurry. The sweating fever came up the river, their leech is dead of it, and the sick are lying in the church. Would the colony lend its physician for two days?

[fever,their:industrial] {FACTION}'s doctor at {PLACE} is the one in bed this time, and the flu that put him there is filling the clinic. Their letter asks the colony for someone who can doctor, for two days, and promises to pay.

[fever,their:spacer] The clinic at {PLACE} lost its autodoc to a power surge in the same week a fever came in with an off-world trader. {FACTION} need a medic with steady hands for two days, and they ask the colony.

[flux] Bad water after the rains, {FACTION}'s rider says, and half of {PLACE} is down with the flux. They have the beds and the boiling pots; what they need is someone who knows what to do, for two days, and they ask the colony's healer.

[their:empire] By the hand of the town's steward, the Empire asks a kindness of the colony: its healer, for two days, at the sickhouse of {PLACE}, where the town's own physician has fallen ill. The steward promises the Empire's thanks and its silver.
[their:friend] "{FRIEND_nameDef} will know someone," {FACTION}'s rider from {PLACE} said at the gate. A fever is going round the town, and they need a healer for two days.

li.label: Lend a healer to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider set off back to {PLACE} to say a healer is coming.

li.label: The colony can't spare one
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to nurse their own sick as best they can.

terms.li: One of the colony's people who can doctor (Medicine 6 or more), at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away), staying about two days at the sickhouse. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll come home with about {COUNT} silver and a gift of the town's, a good deal wiser about fevers, and {FACTION} will remember who came. Half the stay earns half the silver.

accepted.li: The colony will lend a healer to {PLACE}. Form a caravan with someone who can doctor, and send it there.

ready.li: The colony's healer has reached {PLACE} and gone straight in among the sick. Keep the caravan there while the work goes on.
[flux] The colony's healer is at {PLACE}, boiling water and handing out salt and broth. Keep the caravan there while the work goes on.

reminder.li: The sick at {PLACE} are still waiting for the colony's healer.

done.li: [worked] The worst of the fever has broken at {PLACE}, and nobody else died after the colony's healer came. {FACTION} sent them home with silver, a gift of the town's, and more blessings than the packs could hold.
[worked,flux] The flux has run its course at {PLACE}, and the colony's healer is coming home tired, paid, and loaded with the town's thanks and a gift of theirs.
[partial] The colony's healer did what two short days allowed at {PLACE}, and {FACTION} paid them half and thanked them for every hour.

fail.li: [missed] No healer came from the colony, and {PLACE} buried more of its people than it had to. {FACTION} will not forget who promised and stayed home.

cancelled.li: The sickhouse at {PLACE} no longer looks to the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.

texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} asks, on behalf of {FACTION}'s young, for a learned one of the colony's to teach a day and a half at the town.

[their:tribal] {FACTION}'s old teller of {PLACE} died in the winter, and nobody else knows the counting-knots and the long tellings well enough to pass them on. They ask the colony for someone learned to sit with their young for a day and a half, and to teach what they can.

[their:medieval] {FACTION} have built a school at {PLACE} and have no master for it until the spring. Their letter asks for a learned one of the colony's to teach letters and sums to the children for a day and a half, so the year isn't wasted.

[their:industrial] The schoolteacher at {PLACE} took a job in the city, and {FACTION} have a room of children and a shelf of books and nobody to put them together. Could the colony lend someone learned for a day and a half to start them off?

[their:spacer] The teaching machine at {PLACE} has been down since the flare, and {FACTION}'s young are running wild. They ask the colony for someone who knows things, the old-fashioned way, for a day and a half of lessons.

[their:empire] The town's lady of {PLACE} asks the colony for a scholar to give her household's pages and the town's children a day and a half of lessons, as is fitting in a town of the Empire. She offers silver and a gift in return.

li.label: Lend someone learned to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider went home with the colony's yes.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s young will have to wait.

terms.li: One of the colony's learned people (Intellectual 7 or more), at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away), staying about a day and a half to teach their young. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll come home with about {COUNT} silver and a gift of the town's, and {FACTION} will remember who came. Half the stay earns half the silver.

accepted.li: The colony will lend a teacher to {PLACE}. Form a caravan with someone learned, and send it there.

ready.li: The colony's teacher has reached {PLACE}, and there are already children waiting on the steps. Keep the caravan there while the lessons go on.
[their:tribal] The colony's teacher is at {PLACE}, sitting in a ring of {FACTION}'s young by the fire. Keep the caravan there while the lessons go on.

reminder.li: The children at {PLACE} are still waiting for the colony's teacher.

done.li: [worked] The colony's teacher left {PLACE} with a crowd of children walking them to the edge of town, each reciting something. {FACTION} paid in silver and a gift of their own making, and asked when they might come again.
[partial] The colony's teacher gave the children at {PLACE} what lessons there was time for. {FACTION} paid half and kept the slates.

fail.li: [missed] No teacher came from the colony, and the children of {PLACE} were sent back to the fields. {FACTION} remember who said yes.

cancelled.li: The school at {PLACE} no longer looks to the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.

texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} writes that {FACTION} will make peace with an old rival at the town, and asks the colony to send someone of good name to stand witness for half a day.

[truce,their:tribal] {FACTION} and a band they have fought with over the grazing will make peace at {PLACE}, by the fire, with a spear broken between them. Both sides want a witness who belongs to neither. {FACTION} ask the colony for {A_nameDef}, or another with a good tongue, for half a day.

[truce,their:medieval] {FACTION} will seal a truce at {PLACE} with the men of the next valley, and the custom is that a stranger of good name sets a mark beside the seals. They ask the colony for its best speaker, for half a day.

[truce,their:hightech] {FACTION} and a rival town are signing a ceasefire at {PLACE}, and both want a neutral signature on it that neither side can call bought. Their letter asks the colony for someone respected, for half a day.

[boundary] Two villages of {FACTION} have quarrelled over a stream for three generations, and they have finally agreed where the line runs. They want a witness from outside to walk it with them at {PLACE} and say so, for half a day.

[truce,their:empire] A truce will be sworn at {PLACE} before the Empire's herald between the town's knight and a neighbouring lord. Custom asks a witness of no house, and the herald asks the colony for one of good name, for half a day, with the Empire's thanks.
[their:friend] "Bring {FRIEND_nameDef}," {FACTION}'s letter asks. "Both sides know {FRIEND_objective}." They need a witness at {PLACE} for half a day.

li.label: Send a witness to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider went home to say the colony will stand witness.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: {FACTION} will find another witness, or wait.

terms.li: One of the colony's people with a good name and a good tongue (Social 6 or more), at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away), staying about half a day while it is done. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll come home with about {COUNT} silver, and {FACTION} will remember who stood witness. Half the time earns half.

accepted.li: The colony will send a witness to {PLACE}. Form a caravan with one of its best speakers, and send it there.

ready.li: The colony's witness has reached {PLACE}, where both sides are waiting. Keep the caravan there while it is done.
[boundary] The colony's witness is at {PLACE}, walking the stream with the elders of both villages. Keep the caravan there while it is done.

reminder.li: Both sides are waiting at {PLACE} for the colony's witness.

done.li: [worked,truce] It is done at {PLACE}, and the colony's witness stood between the two sides while it was. {FACTION} paid them in silver and will tell the story of the day with the colony in it.
[worked,boundary] The line is walked and marked at {PLACE}, with the colony's witness at the head of it. {FACTION} paid them, and both villages say it is fair.
[worked,their:empire] The truce is sworn at {PLACE}, and the herald entered the colony's witness in the roll by name. The Empire paid them, and its honour is satisfied.
[partial] The colony's witness had to leave {PLACE} before it was all done. {FACTION} paid half, and finished it with someone else.

fail.li: [missed] No witness came from the colony, and the two sides at {PLACE} stood looking at each other until someone went home. {FACTION} remember whose seat was empty.

cancelled.li: The business at {PLACE} no longer needs the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.

texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} writes that the town's tools are past mending by its own hands this season, and asks the colony for a smith for a day at their forge.

[harvest] {FACTION}'s smith at {PLACE} broke an arm, and the harvest is close with half the sickles blunt and three scythes cracked. They ask the colony for someone who can work metal for a day at their forge, and they will pay.

[plough] The ground at {PLACE} is ready for the plough, and {FACTION}'s ploughshares are not: bent, cracked and rusted through the winter. They ask the colony for a smith for a day at their forge before the sowing slips past.

[machines] The pumps and the old tractor at {PLACE} have both broken in the same week, and {FACTION}'s mechanic has gone to the city for parts that won't come. They ask the colony for someone handy with tools for a day.

[their:empire] The steward of {PLACE} writes on the knight's behalf. The town's armourer is away with the levy, and the tools and the pumps need seeing to. Would the colony lend its smith for a day? The Empire pays fairly.

li.label: Lend a smith to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider went home to say a smith is coming.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will make do with blunt tools.

terms.li: One of the colony's people who can work metal and tools (Crafting 6 or more), at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away), staying about a day at their forge or their workshop. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll come home with about {COUNT} silver and a gift of the town's, and {FACTION} will remember who came. Half the day earns half.

accepted.li: The colony will lend a smith to {PLACE}. Form a caravan with someone who can work metal, and send it there.

ready.li: The colony's smith has reached {PLACE} and already has the forge roaring. Keep the caravan there while the work goes on.
[machines] The colony's mechanic is at {PLACE}, flat on their back under the first of the pumps. Keep the caravan there while the work goes on.

reminder.li: The broken tools at {PLACE} are still waiting for the colony's smith.

done.li: [worked] Every blade at {PLACE} has an edge on it again, and the colony's smith is coming home with silver and a gift of the town's. {FACTION} say the harvest will be in on time.
[worked,machines] The pumps at {PLACE} are running and the tractor coughed into life at the third try. {FACTION} paid the colony's mechanic and gave them a gift of the town's for the road.
[partial] The colony's smith mended what a short stay allowed at {PLACE}. {FACTION} paid half, and will finish the rest by hand.

fail.li: [missed] No smith came from the colony, and {PLACE} went into the season with broken tools. {FACTION} remember who said they'd come.

cancelled.li: The forge at {PLACE} no longer looks to the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.

texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} asks the colony, in {FACTION}'s name, to keep a store of theirs dry and safe in its own stockpiles for a season, for a fee.

[grain] {FACTION}'s granary at {PLACE} has a cracked wall and rats in the cracks, and they won't have it rebuilt before the season turns. They ask the colony to keep part of their grain dry in its own stores until they can fetch it, and they will pay for the keeping.

[timber] {FACTION} have felled more timber at {PLACE} than their yard will hold, and it needs to season under cover. Could the colony keep a stack of it in its stores for a season? Their carts would bring it and fetch it, and they'd pay for the room.

[iron,their:hightech] {FACTION}'s depot at {PLACE} has been broken into twice this month, and they want their steel somewhere the thieves don't know about. They ask the colony to keep a load of it for a season, for a fee.

[iron,their:lowtech] {FACTION}'s smithy at {PLACE} has more iron than it can work before the spring, and nowhere safe to keep it. They ask the colony to hold a load of their metal for a season, for a fee.

[cloth] The flood ran through {FACTION}'s weaving sheds at {PLACE}, and the bolts that were spared need a dry roof until the sheds are mended. They ask the colony to keep them for a season, for a fee.

[their:empire] The steward of {PLACE} asks, on behalf of the town's knight, that the colony keep a part of the Empire's stores in its own for a season while the town's are rebuilt, and offers a fee fitting the Empire's dignity.

li.label: Keep it for them
li.outcome: The rider went home to say the colony has room.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to find room somewhere else.

terms.li: {FACTION}'s carts bring {ITEM} to the colony's gate, and come back for as much at the end of the season the Quests tab shows. Keep it in the stockpiles meanwhile: what is in the stores then counts, the colony's own the same as theirs.\n\nFor the keeping they'll pay {COUNT} silver. Whatever is short, the colony pays for in silver at its plain worth; without the silver, they take what there is, and remember it.

[grain] {FACTION}'s carts bring {ITEM} to the colony's gate, and come back for as much at the end of the season the Quests tab shows. Keep it dry and out of the heat in the stockpiles meanwhile: what is in the stores then counts, the colony's own the same as theirs.\n\nFor the keeping they'll pay {COUNT} silver. Whatever has spoiled or gone into the pot, the colony pays for in silver at its plain worth; without the silver, they take what there is, and remember it.

accepted.li: The colony will keep {FACTION}'s store. Their carts are bringing {ITEM} to the gate: see it into the stockpiles.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s carts come back soon for {ITEM}, and the stores are short of it.

done.li: [kept] {FACTION}'s store is all in the stockpiles just as they left it, and their carts are coming to take it home, with {ITEM} silver for the keeping. {PLACE} will remember the colony kept its word.
[madegood] Some of {FACTION}'s store is gone from the stockpiles. Their carts are coming for what there is, and for {ITEM} silver from the colony's stores to make the rest good at its plain worth.

fail.li: [short] {ITEM} of {FACTION}'s store is gone from the stockpiles, and the colony hasn't the silver to make it good. Their carts are coming for what there is, and {PLACE} will hear all about it.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} have broken with the colony. Their store is left where it lies.

texts.li: [host] {HOST} of {PLACE} writes to ask the colony to raise {BEAST}, a young {THING} of the town's, through the season, and promises its keep.

[foal] {FACTION}'s best mare at {PLACE} died foaling, and the foal, {BEAST}, is too much for their stable this season. Their drover asks if the colony will raise {BEAST} until it is strong enough to come home, and the town will pay for its keep.

[calf] {FACTION} have a young {THING} at {PLACE} named {BEAST}, the last of a good line, and nothing left to feed it on through the season after the blight took the hay. They ask the colony to raise it for them and send it home well, and they'll pay.

[kid] A sickness is going through {FACTION}'s flock at {PLACE}, and they want their best young {THING}, {BEAST}, kept well away from it. Will the colony keep {BEAST} for a season? Their drover will bring it and fetch it.

[pup] {FACTION}'s herders at {PLACE} need a working dog for next year, and {BEAST}, the pup they picked, needs a season of growing up with other people's animals. They ask the colony to keep {BEAST}, and they'll pay for the trouble.

[their:empire] The town's knight at {PLACE} asks the colony to raise {BEAST}, a young {THING} of the Empire's stables, through the season while the stables are rebuilt. The steward promises payment fitting the Empire's honour.
[skill:Animals] {FACTION}'s drover asked for {A_nameDef} by name: they have heard the colony is good with animals. {BEAST}, a young {THING} from {PLACE}, needs raising for a season, and they'll pay.

li.label: Raise {BEAST} for them
li.outcome: The drover went home to fetch {BEAST}.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will find another place for {BEAST}.

terms.li: {FACTION}'s drover walks {BEAST} in to the colony's gate and hands it over. From then it is the colony's to feed and keep until the drover comes back at the end of the season the Quests tab shows.\n\nKept well (fed, not sick, no wound left untended), {BEAST} is worth {COUNT} silver to them; kept poorly, half. If {BEAST} dies or is lost, they'll take it hard.

accepted.li: The colony will raise {BEAST}. {FACTION}'s drover is bringing the young {THING} to the gate.

ready.li: {FACTION}'s drover handed {BEAST} over at the gate and went back up the road. The young {THING} is the colony's to keep well until they come for it.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s drover will come back for {BEAST} soon.

done.li: [returned] {BEAST} has grown glossy and sure on its legs at the colony, and {FACTION}'s drover is on the road to lead the young {THING} home, with {ITEM} silver for its keep.
[poorly] {BEAST} has not done well at the colony, and {FACTION} have heard. Their drover is coming to lead it home, with {ITEM} silver, half what was promised.
[bonded] {FACTION} sent word that {BEAST} follows {A_nameDef} about like a shadow now, and they won't part them. The colony keeps {BEAST}, and {PLACE} counts it a kindness done both ways.

fail.li: [died] {BEAST}, the young {THING} {FACTION} trusted to the colony, is dead. {PLACE} took the news badly.
[lost] {BEAST} is no longer the colony's to give back. {FACTION} have sent word, and it is not a kind one.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} have broken with the colony. Whatever becomes of {BEAST} now is the colony's business.

texts.li: A rider from {PLACE} came to the gate in a hurry. {DEAD}, one of {FACTION}'s old ones, has been forgetting things all year, and yesterday walked out of the house in a nightshirt and didn't come back. The footprints go onto the colony's land.\n\n{FACTION} are searching their own side of the hill. They ask the colony to search its own.

[their:lowtech] {FACTION}'s herder from {PLACE} says {DEAD}, an old shepherd who has walked these hills for sixty years, went out with the flock and came back without either. The flock came home. {DEAD} didn't, and the tracks lead onto the colony's land.

[their:hightech] {FACTION} sent word from {PLACE}: {DEAD}, an old man of the town who gets lost in his own street these days, walked off the bus at the wrong stop yesterday and hasn't been seen since. Someone saw him heading onto the colony's land.
[their:friend] {FACTION}'s rider asked for {FRIEND_nameDef}. {DEAD}, one of their old ones, is lost somewhere on the colony's land, and they trust no one more to find {X_objective}.

li.label: Find {DEAD}
li.outcome: The colony has taken it on.

li.label: The colony can't spare anyone
li.outcome: The rider turned back without a word.

terms.li: Find {DEAD} somewhere on the colony's land before the trail goes cold. Anyone of the colony who comes within a few steps of {X_objective}, in sight, will find {X_objective}; then {DEAD} will follow them back, and {FACTION} will come for {X_objective}.\n\n{FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver, and never forget who found {X_objective}.

accepted.li: The colony is searching for {DEAD}. Someone has to come within a few steps of {X_objective}, somewhere out on the colony's land.

ready.li: {A_nameDef} found {DEAD} sitting on a stone, talking to nobody in particular about a dog that died forty years ago. {DEAD} is coming back to the colony on {A_nameDef}'s arm, and {FACTION} are sending someone for {X_objective}.

reminder.li: {DEAD} is still out there somewhere, and the trail won't stay warm much longer.

done.li: [found] {DEAD}'s kin are on their way with a blanket and a scolding, to walk {X_objective} home between them. {FACTION} send {ITEM} silver in thanks, and {PLACE} will know that {A_nameDef} found their old one.

fail.li: [searchers] {FACTION}'s own searchers found {DEAD} in the end, cold and confused, far out on the colony's land. They're glad. They're not glad about the colony.
[harmed] {DEAD} didn't make it home. {FACTION} will grieve, and remember it happened on the colony's land.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony, and have taken over the search themselves.

texts.li: [their:lowtech] {FACTION}'s rider from {PLACE} says {DEAD}, one of their hunters, went after a wounded stag two days ago and never came home. {DEAD} knows the hills, but these aren't {X_possessive} hills: the tracks go onto the colony's land.\n\nThey ask the colony to look on its own side.

[their:hightech] {FACTION} sent word from {PLACE}: {DEAD}, a hunter of theirs, went out two days ago after game and hasn't answered a call since. The last anyone heard, {X_pronoun} was somewhere on the colony's land. They ask the colony to look.

[winter] {DEAD}, a trapper of {FACTION}, went out along the trap lines from {PLACE} and didn't come back in, and there's snow in the wind. The lines run onto the colony's land, and {FACTION} ask the colony to look there.
[their:friend] {FACTION}'s rider asked for {FRIEND_nameDef}: {DEAD}, one of their hunters, is lost on the colony's land, and {FRIEND_nameDef} knows it best.

li.label: Find {DEAD}
li.outcome: The colony has taken it on.

li.label: The colony can't spare anyone
li.outcome: The rider turned back without a word.

terms.li: Find {DEAD} somewhere on the colony's land before the trail goes cold. Anyone of the colony who comes within a few steps of {X_objective}, in sight, will find {X_objective}; then {DEAD} will follow them back, and {FACTION} will come for {X_objective}.\n\n{FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver, and remember who found their hunter.

accepted.li: The colony is searching for {DEAD}. Someone has to come within a few steps of {X_objective}, somewhere out on the colony's land.

ready.li: {A_nameDef} found {DEAD} by a dead fire, sore-footed and sheepish and very hungry. {DEAD} is coming back to the colony with {A_objective}, and {FACTION} are sending someone for {X_objective}.

reminder.li: {DEAD} is still out there somewhere, and the trail won't stay warm much longer.

done.li: [found] {DEAD}'s people are on their way to take {X_objective} home, and they will tease {X_objective} about the stag the whole road. {FACTION} send {ITEM} silver, and {PLACE} will know that {A_nameDef} found their hunter.

fail.li: [searchers] {FACTION}'s own people found {DEAD} in the end, limping home on the far side of the colony's land. They're glad. They're not glad about the colony.
[harmed] {DEAD} didn't make it home. {FACTION} will grieve, and remember it happened on the colony's land.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony, and have taken over the search themselves.

texts.li: [trader] {FACTION}'s rider says {DEAD}, a trader of theirs, sold a whole season's goods on the coast and must carry the silver home to {PLACE}. The road passes where bandits were seen last month, and {DEAD} won't take it alone. Could the colony's caravan walk with {X_objective}?

[healer] {DEAD}, a healer of {FACTION}, is needed at {PLACE} and is coming by way of the colony. {X_pronoun} has a pack of medicines worth stealing and no weapon to speak of, and {FACTION} ask whether the colony's caravan might see {X_objective} the rest of the way.

[scholar] {DEAD}, a scholar of {FACTION}, is carrying a chest of old books back to {PLACE}, and has been robbed of one chest already on the way. {FACTION} ask the colony's caravan to walk the last stretch with {X_objective}.

[their:empire] By leave of the town's knight, {DEAD}, a servant of the Empire bound for {PLACE} with letters, asks the colony's escort on the road. The Empire's honour, the steward writes, does not forget such company.

li.label: See {DEAD} to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The rider went to tell {DEAD} the colony will see {X_objective} home.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {DEAD} will have to wait for other company, or risk the road alone.

terms.li: {DEAD} comes to the colony and waits there. Any caravan of the colony's, with one of its own people, that sets out from the colony for {PLACE} (about {TALE} away) takes {X_objective} along; when it gets there, {X_pronoun} is safe.\n\n{FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver at {PLACE}, and remember who walked with {X_objective}.

accepted.li: The colony will walk {DEAD} to {PLACE}. {X_pronoun} is on the way to the colony to wait for the caravan.

ready.li: {DEAD} has come to the colony and is waiting for a caravan to {PLACE}.

reminder.li: {DEAD} is still waiting at the colony for a caravan to {PLACE}.

done.li: [arrived] The road was long and quiet, and {DEAD} talked most of it. At {PLACE}, {FACTION} met the colony's caravan with {ITEM} silver and a good deal of thanks.
[arrived,trader] {DEAD} counted the silver twice at the gate of {PLACE}, all there, and paid the colony's caravan {ITEM} of it on the spot.

fail.li: [alone] No caravan went to {PLACE}, and {DEAD} set off alone in the end. {FACTION} remember who said they'd walk with {X_objective}.
[turned] The colony's caravan turned back, and {DEAD} walked the rest of the road alone. {FACTION} have heard.
[harmed] {DEAD} never reached {PLACE}. {FACTION} will grieve, and remember whose care {X_pronoun} was in.
[late] The colony's caravan took so long that {FACTION} gave {DEAD} up for lost. They're glad of {X_objective}, and not of the colony.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} have broken with the colony, and {DEAD} has gone another way.
